title: Capacity-Aware Remediation Accelerator Runbook
author: Marcus Chen
content:
Overview

This runbook defines the Capacity-Aware Remediation Accelerator (CARA): a prioritized, telemetry-driven playbook and set of automations to accelerate mitigation of capacity-related SLO breaches and near-miss events. CARA focuses on getting services back within SLOs quickly while preserving correctness and minimizing cascading impact on multi-tenant inference workloads.

Use cases
- Sudden throughput surge causing 95th/99th latency SLO erosion for inference endpoints.
- Persistent KV-cache pressure or memory growth leading to OOMs under load.
- Regional capacity exhaustion where failover and graceful degradation are required.
- Embedding-heavy tenants causing disproportionate GPU allocation churn.

Goals
- Reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) for capacity-induced incidents by 40% vs manual runbook.
- Ensure safe automated mitigations cover at least the top 3% of recurring capacity failure modes.
- Provide clear human escalation paths where automated action is unsafe.

Owner and run cadence
- Primary owner: eng-sre (oncall rotation).
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime (performance team), Platform (autoscaler team).
- Runbook review cadence: quarterly or after any incident where CARA mitigations are applied.

Key concepts and signals
- SLOs: latency_p95 <= 200ms (hosted API), latency_p99 <= 450ms, availability >= 99.9% (region).
- Error budget window: 30 days rolling.
- Capacity telemetry sources: token-rate histograms, GPU util (nvidia-smi and exporter), mem pressure, queue length, continuous-batching latency histogram, autoscaler events, KV cache hit ratio.
- Primary signals and thresholds (triggers):
  - latency_p99 > 450ms sustained for 3m -> Tier-2 trigger.
  - request_queue_length > 1000 for 2m -> Tier-2 trigger.
  - GPU_util > 85% for 5m and scaling_events failing -> Tier-1 alert (immediate).
  - OOM_kube_pods >= 1 in last 10m -> Critical.
  - cache_miss_rate increases by >30% above baseline -> Investigate for cold-traffic surge.

Escalation matrix
1) Tier-1 (Critical): page SRE primary. PagerDuty: PD escalation policy "CARA-Tier1".
   - Examples: sustained OOMs, autoscaler stuck, persistent API 500 spikes.
2) Tier-2 (High): notify SRE rotation + runtime on-call via Slack channel #sre-capacity.
3) Tier-3 (Advisory): create incident ticket; follow-up at next capacity retro.

Automated remediation catalog (safe-first order)
1) Soft admission control: reduce new low-priority tokens by 30% for 2 minutes.
   - Command example (control plane): rctl admission set --route="embedding*" --ratio=0.7 --reason="CARA soft admission"
2) Prefix caching warmup: trigger KV prefetch for high-frequency prefixes.
   - Example: curl -X POST https://internal-api/kv/prefetch -d '{"prefixes":["/chat/conv-*"]}'
3) Horizontal scaling override (scale up GPU pool by +1 node):
   - kubectl -n redwood scale nodepool/gpu-pool --replicas=$(($(kubectl get nodepool gpu-pool -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+1))
   - Note: only allowed when autoscaler reports capable of provisioning in <10m.
4) Token priority spill: temporarily demote experimental tenants to best-effort class.
   - CLI: rctl tenant update --tenant-id=tenant-uuid --priority=best-effort --ttl=300
5) Canary fallback model: switch subset of requests to a smaller, quantized variant for degraded latency.
   - Example rollout: curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/rollouts -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","from":"gpt-large","to":"gpt-medium-quant","pct":15}'

Safety & gating rules for automation
- Automation MUST be idempotent and have an automatic rollback path (TTL or explicit health check).
- Any change that affects >= 10% of tenant traffic requires two-step approval unless pre-approved in the Canary Waiver table.
- Automated scale-ups are permitted if provisioning estimate <= 12 minutes and IO budget is not constrained.
- Automation is disabled for customers flagged as "restricted" in customer metadata.

Operational checklist (immediate responder)
1) Validate the alert: confirm telemetry for the last 10 minutes; capture baseline and delta.
2) Identify impacted routes and tenants using the route-telemetry dashboard.
3) Execute safe-first automation (soft admission) and wait 90s; monitor latency_p95/p99 and queue length.
4) If improvement > 30% on p99 within 3m, continue monitoring and schedule follow-up action.
5) If no improvement, escalate to Tier-1 and run scale-up or model-fallback.
6) When capacity is restored, run recovery verification and create a remediation-capture ticket.

Runbook step-by-step (detailed)
1) Triage
   - Open the incident channel: #incident-<service>-<shortid>.
   - Attach links: dashboards (route-level), log search query, latest autoscaler events, recent deploys.
2) Snapshot telemetry
   - Commands:
     - curl "https://telemetry/api/query?range=10m&expr=latency_p99{route=\"/v1/generate\"}" > p99_snapshot.json
     - kubectl get events --namespace inference -o wide --since=10m > kube_events.txt
3) Apply soft mitigations (see automated remediation catalog).
4) If mitigations succeed, mark incident as mitigated and run RCA data collection (see Post-Incident artifacts).
5) If mitigations fail after 10m, trigger manual scale-up and notify platform owners.
6) For regional exhaustion, follow cross-region failover checklist (appendix B).

Post-Incident artifacts and required fields
- Required ticket fields: incident_id, start_time, end_time, top_contributing_signal, automated_actions_taken (list), manual_actions_taken (list), immediate_owner, follow_up_action_items (with owners and due dates), regression_test_prompts (if model fallback occurred).
- Upload artifacts: p99_snapshot.json, kube_events.txt, deployment_hashes.txt, rollout_change_log.md

Verification and rollback tests
- Verification criteria: p95 and p99 returned to within 110% of baseline for 15m, queue length below 25% of pre-incident peak, and no new OOMs for 30m.
- Rollback procedure: reverse in order of application (model fallback -> tenant priority -> soft admission -> scale-up). Each rollback step must be observed for 2m.

Appendix A: Configuration table (thresholds and owners)
| Signal | Tier | Trigger threshold | Auto-action | Owner |
|--------|------|-------------------|-------------|-------|
| latency_p99 | Tier-2 | >450ms for 3m | soft admission -> scale | Runtime oncall |
| request_queue_length | Tier-2 | >1000 for 2m | admission control | Platform |
| gpu_util | Tier-1 | >85% for 5m | scale-up | GPU Fleet |
| OOM_pods | Critical | >=1 in 10m | manual intervention | Runtime oncall |
| cache_miss_rate | Tier-3 | +30% over baseline | prefetch, analyze | Serving Runtime |

Appendix B: Cross-region failover (summary)
1) Verify regional capacity is exhausted (primary signals + cloud provider capacity report).
2) Activate traffic-split policy: route 20% -> secondary region for 10 minutes, observe error rates.
   - CLI: rctl traffic-split set --from-region=us-west-2 --to-region=us-east-1 --ratio=0.2 --ttl=600
3) If stable, increase to 50% over 15 minutes.
4) Coordinate with networking (VPN, DNS TTL) for any required adjustments.

Appendix C: Automation snippets and safety harness
- Example Terraform snippet for pre-emptive GPU pool warmup:
  resource "redwood_nodepool" "gpu_warm" {
    name = "gpu-warmup"
    node_count = 2
    labels = { workload = "serving-warmup" }
  }
- Healthcheck pseudo-script (python):
  import requests
  def check_p99(route):
      r = requests.get(f'https://telemetry/api/p99?route={route}&range=5m')
      return r.json()[0]['value']

Metrics and dashboards to reference
- /dashboards/serving/route-latency (prebaked filter: route=/v1/generate)
- /dashboards/platform/autoscaler-events
- /dashboards/runtime/gpu-utilization

Follow-ups and continuous improvement
- After any CARA use, create a retro ticket and tag with label 'cara-remediation'.
- Quarterly: evaluate which automated mitigations had false positives and tune thresholds to reduce noisy activations.
- Maintain a small simulation lab to rehearse common CARA mitigations without affecting production (see /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/sre-simulation-lab).
